A tower grown entirely beneath the earth, accessible only by descending shaft, its subterranean chambers expanding impossibly downward, phosphorescent fungi illuminating vaulted stone, the deepest room thrumming with pressure from something vast below.

A red sandstone desert tower half-buried in drifting dunes, only two upper storeys exposed, its carved friezes of celestial bodies still precise, its sealed iron door etched with wards no wind in a century has worn.

The private sanctum within a tower's highest room, circular, draped in star-maps and layered carpets, an orrery of gold and dark glass slowly orbiting a suspended amber crystal, the sole source of warm revolving light.

A tower of stacked river-boulders, rough and mossy, each stone impossibly balanced on the next with no mortar visible, defying gravity by obvious enchantment, wild herbs rooting in every gap, smoke rising from a clay chimney.

A glass-and-wrought-iron tower in the fashion of a great lantern, its interior fully visible from outside, shelves and workbenches glowing, the wizard's silhouette moving within like a dark fish in a luminous jar.

A half-submerged tower rising from a flooded forest, waterline staining its stones green to halfway up, upper windows sealed with wax and silence, herons nesting on the battlements above a glassy reflection that shows different skies.
A tall crooked spire of mismatched grey and amber stone leaning improbably against the sky, tiny glowing windows spiralling up its height, a conical slate roof crowned with a pulsing violet orb.

The cluttered circular interior of a wizard's high study, crammed floor-to-ceiling with leaning bookshelves, stoppered jars, hanging herbs and brass instruments, a worn oak desk buried under scrolls at its heart.
A slender crystal tower rising from a misty highland lake, its translucent walls refracting sunlight into drifting prismatic rainbows, ancient arcane runes glowing cold blue deep within its facets.
A floating tower hovering serenely above its own crumbled foundation, great chains of golden light tethering it to the earth below, its windows blazing with restless inner fire.
A gnarled tower grown directly from an enormous living tree, bark walls twisted into arched windows and spiralling stairs, green witchlight flickering between the roots far below.

A vast multi-level library interior stretching impossibly upward, iron spiral staircases threading between packed shelves, enchanted candles drifting at every level, the uppermost reaches lost in warm amber haze.

A ruined half-collapsed mage-tower standing in a field of scorched earth, one wall entirely gone, charred shelves clinging to the interior, arcane sigils still faintly burning on the remaining stonework.
A cliffside tower clinging impossibly to a sheer coastal rock face, its base fused with salt-white stone, narrow arched windows peering over the crashing sea far below.
A black obsidian sorcerer's spire rising from a blasted volcanic plain, its mirror-smooth flanks reflecting the sky in dark distortion, a crown of jagged black finials encircling a skull-pale summit.

The warm candle-lit interior of a tower alchemy laboratory, low curved ceiling hung with drying specimens, a long stone bench crowded with glowing retorts and bubbling alembics, the air thick with sulphur and herbs.
A tower of stacked impossible geometry, each storey rotated and offset from the last, windows facing no consistent direction, the whole structure defying gravity through sheer enchanted stubbornness.
An observatory atop a high tower, a great brass telescope angled through an open dome of riveted copper, charts pinned to every surface, celestial models turning slowly in the draughty dark.
A sea-stack tower, a solitary finger of dark basalt rising from crashing ocean waves, its windows glowing amber against the storm, lightning rods bristling along its salt-pitted upper spire.

A tower of pale bone-white marble veined with gold, perfectly cylindrical and impossibly smooth, its every surface etched with fine astronomical diagrams and conjuration circles that glow at midnight.

The grand interior atrium of a conjurer's tower, a hollow central shaft rising through all floors, ethereal blue light descending from a skylight far above, summoning circles inlaid in the stone floor.
A squat and enormously broad tower of dark mossy granite, wide as a fortress keep, tiny slit windows circling each tier, a flat roof crowded with grotesque weathervane-golems.

A tower carved directly into a glacier's face, its walls translucent green-blue ice veined with silver runes, cold witchlight burning deep within, the whole structure groaning imperceptibly in the mountain wind.

A slender iron tower rising from a city rooftop, its riveted black flanks streaked with verdigris and arcane chalked symbols, thin lightning arcing between its twin antenna spires in constant restless crackle.

The circular interior of a high alchemist's study, shelves of identical black jars labelled in gold, a central worktable with an enormous open grimoire, a single beam of filtered green light from above.

A tower wholly wrapped in climbing enchanted ivy, leaves of deep emerald and midnight purple, small lanterns glowing like fireflies caught in the vines, the stone beneath barely visible beneath the living mass.

A sandstone desert tower half-buried in a vast dune, only its upper third exposed, carved archways sealed with sand-packed sigils, the interior rumoured to still burn with the original mage's ever-lit hearthstone.

A tall spiralling tower built from stacked rings of different coloured stone — red, grey, cream and black — each ring slightly rotated, giving the whole spire a slow corkscrewing silhouette against pale cloud.

A collapsed tower interior still inhabited, the roof long fallen, open to the sky, moss reclaiming the flagstones, a single enchanted workbench inexplicably intact and still covered in active unfinished spellwork.

A vast subterranean tower-shaft descending into the earth rather than rising from it, iron walkways ringing a central chasm, bookshelves and laboratories carved into the sheer rock walls floor after descending floor.

A tower of living silver-grey stone that slowly breathes, its outer walls gently expanding and contracting, windows that open and close like eyes at dusk, runes appearing and fading across its skin in constant slow motion.

A tall crooked spire of mismatched granite and river-stone leaning improbably against the bruised sky, its spiralling windows flickering with cold blue fire, a lopsided conical roof crowned by a slowly rotating brass orrery.

The vast multi-level interior of a library-tower, its iron spiral staircase climbing through galleries of floor-to-ceiling shelves, tomes drifting open in mid-air, globes of magelight bobbing gently among the ascending shadows.
